title: Shared-year samples leave a weak rain-error bound on the 2010-2021 runoff slope loss in 159 south-east Australian catchments
abstract: We test whether rain measurement error alone can explain a late loss of annual runoff response. We prove a necessary reliability bound for two rain products with correlated additive errors and stable gains. We apply it to AGCD, SILO and runoff in 159 south-east Australian catchments. Separate marginal rain slopes compare 1951-1996 with 2010-2021. Late slope retention was 0.772 with AGCD and 0.806 with SILO. Joint samples of shared three-year blocks and spatial cells gave 95% intervals of 0.614-0.966 and 0.641-1.000. The point estimates need uniform error-correlation caps of at least 0.950 and 0.940 before this necessary condition permits an unchanged latent response. But the cap intervals were 0.262-0.983 and 0-0.982. Thus the data do not give a positive shared-error threshold across both products. This does not prove a rain artefact. The test needs classical additive errors, stable gains and a constant latent linear response. It cannot identify a cause or cover changed calibration and nonlinear response. The package includes the proof, input tables, source hashes, code, all samples, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Late slope retention and minimum permitted rain-error correlation, with joint shared-year and spatial-cell 95% intervals. The error bound is necessary, not sufficient.
